en: Having seen that [the teachings] were devoid of refinement, those lowest of men, out of ignorance, brought about the total fragmentation of the commitments on all sides. (12)
Therefore, the power of all mantras has been entirely concealed; by that concealment, those remaining letters are protected as mere phonemes alone. || 13 ||
O Great Goddess, when mantras are employed with their potency concealed even according to the prescribed rite, they do not achieve success for him, even if recited hundreds of millions of times.
Even for one who understands the grasping of that [object] as well as the grasping of a self, and likewise the guru and the even greater guru, accomplishment is not far off. (15)
Having obtained a guru who is devoid of power, practitioners who desire the results described in the Kalpas do not achieve success, even with great effort. ||16||
Therefore, one who has been initiated by the purificatory rites of Śiva and desires spiritual perfection should, having realized the immersion into the power of Rudra, practice its grasping. 17.
One is not initiated here by means of the conventions of the agent, the means of knowledge, and so forth, nor is one ever devoid of the presence of the clarified butter and the fire. ||18||
Mental [offerings] are praised for rites performed for specific desires by those who long for liberation; some here desire them in the Śaiva tradition, but never in the Bhairava [tradition]. (19)

Having observed on all sides the decline of human beings' formative predispositions (*saṃskāra*) and the fragmentation of the conventions (*samaya*), those lowest of men have concealed the power (*vīrya*) of all mantras.
When that [initiation] is guarded, the remaining castes are merely guarded;
however, having seen the distinction between the ignorant and the wise, the mantras have been strictly concealed.
One who knows them as guarded understands his own spiritual heritage and, desiring success from the teacher, attains it through the true nature of unwavering absorption by any means whatsoever.

Therefore, the secret of the mantras has been well-guarded by him; thus, those who do not desire the acceptance of the *vāma* [path], nor the descent (*samāveśa*) of Śiva from afar, and who are in no way devoid of the true nature of the fire, should serve Bhairava with their minds in the Śaiva tradition. [Chapter] The Goddess said: That which was proclaimed as "acceptance" (*graha*), as well as the "acceptance of the self" (*ātmaparigraha*), and the teacher (*guru*) and the most eminent teacher (*gurutara*)—by knowing these, perfection (*siddhi*) is desired. (1)
Bhairava said: The mantra is to be known as most weighty; the guru is called the teacher (ācārya). ||2||
By that, as soon as one has been initiated, there occurs the appropriation of the self; O fair-faced one, through its grasping, the attainment of the true essence of mantra occurs here.
One should observe the characteristic of divine conduct in the teacher due to his immersion in the power of Rudra; it is taught that the reception of the mantra occurs therein. ||4||
Through the immersion into the power of Rudra, the power of the great-souled teacher arises swiftly, producing immediate conviction. ||5||
The first characteristic proclaimed is unwavering devotion to Rudra; the second is the accomplishment of the mantra, which produces immediate conviction. ||6||

The third is the state of being obedient to all sentient beings by doing whatever they require; the fourth characteristic is remembered as the completion of the task once it has been undertaken. ||7||
The fifth is declared to be the power of poetry, which is charming and adorned with poetic figures; it is remembered as the fifth characteristic, which paralyzes the eloquence of others. ||8||
Thus has this fivefold characteristic of the teacher been declared; one who is thus endowed with these characteristics is a knower of initiation and a knower of reality.
He who knows the secret maṇḍala-sūtras, who acts for the benefit of the world, and who, through the penetration of Rudra’s power, grants the desires of his devotees. ||10||
O Dear One, he in whom this immersion into the power of Rudra is observed is declared to be a Guru equal to me, the illuminator of the potency of mantra. (11)
cf.
"In this regard, the first sign is unwavering devotion to Rudra" (Mālinīvijayottara). cf.

"And mastery over all sentient beings is remembered as the third characteristic" (Mālinīvijayottara). "The accomplishment of the task already undertaken is said to be the fourth sign" (Mālinīvijayottara). cf.

The accomplishment of mantras, mastery over all principles (*tattvas*), the perfection of ritual actions, and poetic skill—this fifth [accomplishment] should be known as charming and adorned with ornaments. In the *Mālinīvijayottara*, the "seizing" (*graha*) has been fully explained. When the mantra is known by those who have realized it, it becomes exceedingly weighty; through that, the teacher (*ācārya*) becomes the "seizer. By means of the true state (*sadbhāva*) and immersion (*samāveśa*), this is the characteristic of the teacher; therein lies the seizing through immersion, which produces immediate conviction. Devotion to Rudra, power in Rudra, and union with Rudra result in immediate submissiveness. The completion of what has been undertaken is declared to be poetic skill; when joined with poetic skill, it is endowed with ornaments for the sake of the knower. Through immersion, the bestower of power to devotees is perceived; O Beloved, the Guru is seen to be adorned and equal to the Supreme Guru. Having obtained one who is even more weighty than the Guru, and remaining steadfast in his acceptance, the devotee—even in every circumstance—attains success in a short time. (12)
Those of small intelligence, who have taken up discipleship under a guru who lacks the aforementioned characteristics and who have themselves received the mantra, suffer. (13)
Thus addressed by the high-souled Bhairava, the Great Goddess prostrated herself and again spoke these words to the Teacher of the World: ||14||
The Goddess said: "It is even so, O Mahādeva; the reality is not otherwise. Just as it was asked, it has been explained from the beginning in its proper sequence. (15)
However, this scripture is declared to be partless and worshipped by the best of gods; for the Guru is considered the primary [authority], and he is difficult to find in the worlds. ||16||
Therefore, O best of gods, please speak hereafter of the Siddhayogeśvarīmata, which is free from all pretenses and bestows all accomplishments.
By the mere perception of which, men who are devoted to recitation and meditation—though devoid of vows and sacrifices—attain success without any difficulty whatsoever. (18)
Thus addressed by the goddess Bhairavī, Bhairava spoke these words: Bhairava said: "Listen, O beloved, I shall proclaim that which bestows the fruit of all desires. (19)
The system of the Siddhayogeśvarīs, however, is the accomplishment of mantra, which, when combined with recitation and meditation, produces immediate conviction. ||20||
O fair-faced one, Rudra-śakti is declared to be the source of all those renowned, mighty female lords of yoga (yogeśvarī). 21.
Empowered by that very [power], those beings sport without hesitation; she remains pervading all this in both supreme and non-supreme forms. 22.
She is renowned as Yogeśvarī; O Dear One, her form is threefold. I shall explain their distinctions, according to how they are established throughout the universe. (23)

In this very way, [the teaching] was spoken by the Guru when he was established [in that state]. O God, from the beginning, it has been proclaimed; it is honored and esteemed. It is considered the Guru, and thus it is said. Without artifice, O Yogīśvarī, it is the means by which [liberation] is attained. Those who are devoid of it are excluded. Without any affliction, it has been declared by the Goddess. Whatever [powers] there may be, as they are celebrated, some are the source of sovereignty. By her alone they are empowered. Those beings who are free from doubt, through this form, [attain] everything. O Dear One, they are established in the All, even in the destitute. Immediately, having wiped away the darkness of ignorance residing in the body of the bound soul (paśu), those powers which bestow grace are the givers of Śiva. 24.
Presided over by those non-terrible powers (śaktis), the Rudras, whose minds are ever dedicated to Sadāśiva, liberate the individual soul (aṇu) from bondage. ||25||
But they are remembered as "terrible" because they obstruct the path to liberation. ||26||
Possessed by those powers, the Rudras, who cause the creation and dissolution of the world, sport within their own bodies like children with soft bulls.
Those [passions] which cause the downward flow of the stream, even while they delight the person in sensual enjoyments, also bind the person to the state of a beast. (28)
But those [powers] which obstruct the path to liberation are remembered as most terrible; Rudras, whose consciousness has been strengthened, are presided over by them. ||29||

Even those who are deeply attached to the enjoyments of cattle (worldly existence) are made to fall lower and lower; yet, because the immersion into the three powers is everywhere Śaṅkara (the Beneficent One). ||30||
They are proclaimed as Ghorā, Ghoratarā, Aghorā, and Aghorās; thus are the guardians of the worlds established through the powers of Rudra. ||31||
Through the division of superior and inferior, the entire host of Yogīśvarīs is empowered by her alone; thus, they all attain accomplishment, possessing overwhelming power. ||32||
She is the source of all powers, and she is celebrated in the Tantras as thirty-eight syllables; she is held to be the embodiment of the Vidyā. ||33||

Having wiped [the face], those powers (*śakti*)—which are formidable, yet not terrifying (*aghorā*)—liberate the individual soul (*aṇu*) from its bonds when the mind is fixed upon them. Those who are obstructive (*nirodhinī*) cause the soul to be blocked; through their ferocity, they cause it to be afflicted. Possessed by them, the one who is neither mild nor terrible indeed sports within the body. Those who, by means of the power that bestows [results], cause the person to be colored by enjoyments while in the state of a bound soul (*paśu*), are empowered and supported. The immersion (*samāveśa*) below and below is everywhere; those [powers] are formidable, and the group (*gaṇa*) is protective. Empowered by that very [power], the womb (*yoni*) consists of thirty and two half-syllables. Its other cause should be known in brief: it is remembered as the supreme and non-supreme state, the cause of all accomplishments (*siddhi*). ||34||
The eight [powers] arising from her possession grant success in yoga; she is proclaimed as being like Tyogeśvarī and like a mother to them all. //35//
For this general characteristic has been proclaimed here in brief; however, the subtle Vaiśeṣika doctrine will be examined further below. ||36||

The lower [speech] is to be known as consisting of three syllables, endowed with words of half-syllables; the higher, however, is to be known as consisting of a single syllable, which produces immediate realization. ||37||
O fair-faced one, she is the goddess consisting of all syllables, the bestower of all accomplishments for all mantras and vidyās. (38)
O beautiful lady, that very energy which has been projected into them is the cause of accomplishment; it is joined with the eight forms by means of its own essential nature. (39)
Endowed with five limbs and adorned by the world-protectors, that goddess is accomplished without a doubt as soon as she is known. ||40||

When excretion has occurred, the great multitude of her mantras and mudrās, as well as the entire host of vidyās that bestow the fruits of all desires, immediately enters her mouth, characterized by the penetration of one's own body.

The two should be known as the "pada" (foot) and the "veśa" (entry), proclaimed like a house on fire; that which is proclaimed as "sūkṣma" (subtle) is considered to be "apada" (without feet). O Goddess, she who is adorned with limbs and members through the meaning of the "pada" form is immediately realized and perfected when practiced; thus the *gaṇa* and the entire *lakṣaṇa* are established. Bhairava said:
Now, therefore, O fair-faced one, I shall fully explain the extraction of the mantras for all three Śaktis, in brief and not in detail. (1)
O Dear One, this supreme secret transmitted through the lineage destroys delusion; having known it, recited it, and meditated upon it, one shall indeed become a possessor of accomplishment. ||2||
Mantras that have extra syllables or are deficient do not bestow results; they become devoid of power, just as has been stated previously. (3)
On a level, pure, well-smeared, and well-protected area of ground, provided with fragrant incense and strewn with heaps of flowers; ||4||
Having fasted for a day and night, adorned with the fragrance of excellent incense, the Guru—with his body anointed with sandalwood—should be fully engaged in the heroic practice (vīrasādhana). ||5||
Accompanied by heroic practitioners who have exerted themselves in the syllables of the mantra and are well-armed with the limbs of the Vidyā, one should draw the power of Rudra.
The Goddess consists of all syllables and is adorned with all phonemes; the head is said to be the letter *tha*, and the two eyes are situated on both sides of the letter *dha*.

The letter *ī* is said to be her nose, facing downwards; the *bindu* is situated in its center. The letter *ba* is known as her face, and the *ka*-group (*kavarga*) is remembered as her teeth in the throat. ||8||

The tongue is designated as the [A-]vāk; the crest-lock (śikhā) is remembered as not facing downwards. The two ears are remembered as the seventh [letter], Jha; their ornaments are the two letters following them (I and Pa). 9.
The first is declared to be the right [arm], and the left is remembered as the second; these two are designated as the arms, and the hands are the seventh.

Bhairava said: The secret means of eradication (*nirṇāsanam*) is not [found] by the mere combination of the three; for mantras are rendered ineffective when deprived of it. As has been declared, when one is situated in a pure, well-prepared, and crowded place, having fasted for a day and night, adorned, and well-armored, he should take that supreme, radiant spear (*śakti*) and place it upon his head along with its limbs. That limb is [to be placed] on the two sides... (conj.). [The syllables] *bindu* (D) and *bindu* (N). In the middle (D) and *mapya* (N), corrected to *gau* (D) and *sau* (N). Regarding *ba*, see *Mālinīvijayottara* 3.38a = *Tantrāloka* 15.122a. *tha* (D) and *tha* (N); *kanthe* (D) and *kantha* (N). *daśanāḥ* (corrected from *daśanā*) (D) and *daśanā* (N); *vāk* (corrected from *vāg*)—see *Mālinīvijayottara* 3.38ab = *Tantrāloka* 15.122ab: *vāt* (D) and *van* (N). *smṛtā* (corrected from *smṛtāḥ*) (D) and *smṛtāḥ* (N). *jhasaptamam* (corrected)—see *Mālinīvijayottara* 3.37d = *Tantrāloka* 15.121d: *sasaptamam* (D) and *smṛtau* (N). *karṇau* (corrected from *smrto karṇā*) (N) and *smrtahkarno* (D). *iparau* (D) and *iparauhḥ* (N). *aparah* (D) and *apara* (N). *dadhau bāhvoḥ samākhyātau* (corrected)—see *Mālinīvijayottara* 3.38d = *Tantrāloka* 15.122d: *rūdho bãhvo samakhyātā* (N) and *rūdho bähvo samakhyātah* (D). *saptamah* (N) and *saptamam* (D). 11. The two syllables *jha* and *ña* should be known as the fingers of both hands. The skull is located on the left hand; this is proclaimed as being preceded by the hand.
In the right hand, the seventh is to be known as the trident-staff (śūladaṇḍa), and the eighth is said to be from the letter *ka*; above that is the actual trident (śūla).
The third eye is said to be on the forehead, O fair-faced one; and the group of four neuter vowels is proclaimed as the garland of the head. 13.
The letter *ṣa* is known as his stomach, *pa* as the heart, and *kṣa* as the navel; furthermore, these two letters, *bha* and *ya*, are to be known respectively as the two peaks of the arms. ||14||

That [syllable] with the visarga in the center of the heart is proclaimed as the Self (ātman); the letter *ha*, however, is declared to be the vital breath (*prāṇa*) residing throughout the entire body. || 15 ||
On the hips it is "ma," while on the secret place it is proclaimed with the anusvāra; below that, O fair-faced one, is the well-known "tā" in the shape of the thighs. 16.

O Dear One, the vowels *e* and *ai* are declared to be in the region of the knees in sequence; following those two, both *o* and *au* are traditionally remembered as being in the shanks in their respective order. 17.

The two *daphau* are declared to be the feet; one should imagine them as before. The two *chalau* are the breasts in sequence, and the *āpayaḥ* situated therein is traditionally known as the milk. ||18||
Thus, by means of the correct procedure, one should draw the power of Rudra, the Goddess who consists of all syllables; thereafter, one should extract the mantras.

That which is [the letter] *ya* is said to be the *prāṇa* (life-force); it is the supreme [element]. The *prāṇa* is said to be the phoneme *ha*. The letters *ma*, *sa*, *ta*, and *tha* reside in the two secret places, the two thighs, and the pair of knees. The feet are *da* and *pha*; the heart is *pa*; the two breasts are *cha* and *la*; and the milk is *ā*. The letters *jha* and *ña* are the trident; the staff is *śa*. Above that is the *mālā* (garland), which is proclaimed as the neuter. The belly is said to be *sa*; the *pa* is attached to the heart. The letter *kṣa* goes to the navel. The arms are formed by the sequence of *ba* and *ha*. The letter *ha* with the *visarga* is declared to be the *prāṇa*. Having extracted the *aparā* (lower) energy along with the *anusvāra* from the hips, the practitioner of mantra (*mantrī*) should again extract the *parā* (supreme) energy, which accomplishes all desires and goals. The letters *e* and *ai* are declared to be the bow in their respective order. Between those two, in due sequence, are *da* and *pha*.
