Bhairava said:

Having fulfilled the vow of the vidyā, one should offer [the guest-offering] to whichever deity one wishes to accomplish; for it is from that [deity] that the argha is given. When the argha has been offered, one should recite the supreme mantra. ||1||
Having performed the sacrifice according to the rules, one should commence the preliminary service; having recited [the mantra] nine hundred thousand times, one should be devoted to the fire-ritual.
At the end of the recitation, having performed the sacrifice again, one should begin the practice; or else, O fair-faced one, if the practice is interrupted, one should do so with the Aparā mantra.
He who recites it six hundred thousand times, with his mind absorbed in meditation upon it, performing fire-offerings and always devoted to the practice of the vow; ||4||
Patient, endowed with fortitude, moderate in eating, and with senses restrained—one who has thus performed service should thereafter begin the practice with wealth. ||5||

If the knower of mantras should always desire to accomplish the higher and lower [attainments], he should then perform recitation according to the prescribed rule, which grants the fulfillment of all aims. ||6||
Whether a householder, one observing vows, or one who has taken up the life of celibacy, he should perform service according to the prescribed rule as the means for achieving all accomplishments.

One should recite [the mantra] three hundred thousand times with a focused mind and in meditative absorption; one should meditate on the form previously described, and in this way the practitioner attains success. ||8||
Then, the hero who has performed the service, endowed with courage and firm in his vows, should begin the divine sādhana that brings about all accomplishments. ||9||
Then, having performed eight ten-thousand oblations, and thereafter two ten-thousand oblations of the flesh of the mahāphalgu bird, one should offer ten thousand more without weariness.
On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, having fasted for three nights and gone to the cremation ground at night, he should remain there alone, devoid of companions.
Having become naked with disheveled hair, standing facing the north with his body erect, the practitioner of mantra, perfectly motionless, should recite the Parāparā mantra. 12.

The practitioner, having attained the supreme goal, with a focused mind, a hero, great-souled and of serene intellect, should recite the supreme mantra while performing his duties, always established in the practice of a householder. Having gone at night to a place of heroic power (*kauvīryā*) accompanied by companions, he should recite until the mistresses of yoga (*yogeśvarīs*) have arrived from all directions. Thus, within a month or a fortnight, the mantra is accomplished; the trembling occurs, and the practitioner succeeds. yam japet parām sādhitām ekacittasthito vīraḥ sa mahātmā prasannadhīḥ | tāvad yāvat samāyātā yogeśvaryaḥ samantataḥ ||13|| He who recites the supreme, accomplished [mantra], the hero remaining with one-pointed mind—that great-souled one of clear intellect [should do so] until the mistresses of yoga have arrived from every side. ||13||
And upon seeing their many terrifying forms, one should not feel fear at all, but should rather recollect the vidyā itself. ||14||
Then, having raised a terrible and most dreadful clamor, they fall to the ground and remain there, surrounding the supreme practitioner.
Some had wide-open eyes, some had blood-red elongated eyes; some had the faces of camels and tigers, and others had the faces of donkeys.
Some, O lady of beautiful countenance, were naked with disheveled hair; others were of formidable appearance, highly fortunate, their eyes rolling with intoxication. ||17||
Some had wide eyes and full, uplifted breasts; their limbs were radiant with divine ornaments, and they were the accomplishers of all desires and aims. ||18||
Then, with an unshakable mind, the knower of mantras, having recited the vidyā and paid homage to them, should pierce his own left side. (19)
Having taken the blood arising from that, having filled his cupped hands therewith, and reciting the mantra, he should then cause it to be given to them. ||20||
When the respectful offering (argha) has been given, then those illustrious goddesses, who bestow the fruit of all desires, grant mental accomplishment to the practitioner. ||21||
Acting according to their will, they sport everywhere at their pleasure; impelled by the power of their own faculties, they depart in that very instant.
Having raised a clamor of shouting that was most terrible and exceedingly dreadful.

Falling to the ground, they remain surrounding the Lord of Sadhakas within their enclosure; having paid homage to them by piercing the left side of one's own body, and having offered the *argha* with that [blood] which has arisen from there, one becomes equal to them. Some have full and elevated breasts, some have faces like asses, and some have wide eyes; some have broad limbs. Joining the palms in reverence, one should offer the *vidyā* and the *argha* to these goddesses according to their respective portions and the power of their own capacities. Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the correct procedure for the *aparā* [mantra], which bestows the fruits of worldly enjoyment and liberation, by means of which practitioners attain success.
Constantly dwelling in cremation grounds, observing silence, smeared with ashes, armored by the previously mentioned ritual placement (nyāsa), moderate in diet, and well-restrained. ||2||
One should recite one hundred thousand syllables with an inner self absorbed in that; when three hundred thousand have been recited, one should then offer oblations of *phalgu* wood in sequence.
Having perceived the mighty power of Rudra, perfectly united with the self of the practitioner, in the form of Aghoreśvara, one shall attain accomplishment. ||4||

The practitioner, however, should employ recitation and meditation resembling fire; and at the conclusion of the recitation, one should perform the white [meditation], which is traditionally known as the "nourishment" (āpyāyana) of that very [fire]. ||5||

One who is disciplined should perform the oblation according to the threefold rule; thereafter, I shall explain in brief the nourishment of the powers (*balas*) and the supreme pervasion (*parāvyāpti*). If, by this very procedure, [it is performed] for seven days— ||1||
Having worshipped him with supreme devotion, listen, O beloved, to his accomplishment: when the seventh day has passed, [he perceives] this [goddess] within the heart-lotus.
Meditating upon Japan, he beholds it in its true form; of this there is no doubt. Having seen it, the practitioner truly rises up with his own physical body. ||3||
Then, divine mental perfection proceeds for him; having sported as he desires, he may become endowed with the qualities such as atomization (aṇimā) and the rest. ||4||

O fair-faced one, having attained mastery over the netherworld, the human realm, the celestial, the intermediate space, and the path of the sky, and having obtained yoga everywhere as well as sovereignty over the gods, he may live for as long as he desires; thus, having become [so], he may go wherever he wishes.

Beyond this, having worshipped the pervasion (vyāpti) and performed recitation, one attains success; through its form, one becomes divine, and gains sovereignty and long life in the netherworld and the atmosphere.
The Goddess said:
O Blessed One, Lord of the Gods, Leader of the hosts of Yoginīs, that doctrine of the Siddhayogeśvarīs has been understood by me. ||1||
In that regard, first there would be the question, and after that, the pervasion (vyāpti); from that [arises] the triad of Rudra’s powers, and from that, the fivefold Vidya-aṅga. ||2||
The Lords of the World, the pledges, initiation, the ritual procedure for fire-offerings by me, the vows in the limbs [of yoga], as well as the knowledge-mantras and even the conquest of death; ||3||
O Lord, the characteristics of one whose speech is purified have been duly ascertained; the great initiation has been heard, as well as the supreme ritual of sakalīkaraṇa. ||4||
Now I wish to hear about the Bhairava of immeasurable luster and the group of Mothers established within the Assembly of Sounds (Śabdarāśi). ||5||
For the benefit of the foremost of practitioners, this is the cause of all accomplishments and the collective means for the practice of the three vidyās in this world.
Having heard that, O Mahādeva, I wish to hear the detailed exposition of the means for attaining the Self, as well as the means for attaining one's own [spiritual goal] together with the yogins. (7)
O Lord of Gods, for one who is endowed with vigor and established in the Cakra, that supreme and highest Tantra is intended by the Lord of Yoginīs. || 8 ||
Bhairava said:
Just as the wish-fulfilling gem in the world bestows whatever object is thought of, so too does the Mātṛkā in the world accomplish whatever desired object is sought. ||9||
O lady of excellent hips, that has been told previously according to my capacity; now, Bhairava is proclaimed as it is in the Uttara-tantra.
O Queen of the Gods, that which is established in the city as the cause for the attainment of all siddhis is its head; one should recite [the mantra] joined with that, including the forehead. 11.

In the region of the head, at the forehead, one should likewise place the Bindu and Nāda; furthermore, in that same manner, one should likewise [place] Bhairava together with the Anusvāra, according to the Yoginīmata. ||12||
The nose is established in the letter *a*, while the mouth is auspicious on all sides; the visarga is proclaimed to be the tongue, ever longing for the supreme nectar. ||13||
O fair-faced one, *i* and *ī* are his two eyes in due order; and *u* and *ū*, O lady of virtuous vows, are the two nostrils of that God of gods. (14)

One should likewise imagine the second [vowel] on the forehead and on the face, O Mistress of the City, for it is the cause situated in the region of the head. The nose is proclaimed as *ṛ*; the two cheeks are *ṝ* and *ḷ*; the pair of ears are *ḹ* in sequence; the two lips of the God are *e* and *ai*; and the rows of teeth are *o* and *au*. (15)
The face of Bhairava should thus be fashioned by means of his own powers; thereafter, however, the body of Bhairava is composed of the Goddess.
O Dear One, the eight Mothers, the mothers of the world, are situated in the *kā* group [of consonants], beginning with Brahmāṇī and ending with Aghoreśī.
Beginning from the right shoulder up to the forehead of the Lord is remembered; it is joined with the neck of Dakṣa and is proclaimed to be of the color of smoke (kavaṇṇa). ||18||
The letter *kha* is the color of the body and the many staffs; the letter *ga* is the right hand; all the fingers are the letter *gha*, while the nails are known as the letter *na*. ||19||
O Goddess, O most beautiful one, the *ka*-group has been proclaimed in due order; the neck is placed upon the shoulders, and the letter *ca* is designated as the left. 20.
The letter *cha* shall be the staff-like arms; the letter *ja* is said to be the hands; the letter *jha* is all the fingers; and the letter *ña* is traditionally taught to be the nails. (21)
The syllable *ṭa* is said to be the hips, *tha* the shanks; *ḍa* is the right foot, and *dha* likewise the toes.
By the letter *ṇa*, all the nails are established in the right foot; likewise, the left hip region, the shank, and the foot [are assigned]. (23)
Perform the left [hand gestures] with the *tavarga* in sequence for the fingers and the nails; the *takāra* is proclaimed to be located on the hip. (24)
O Goddess of the Gods, the letter *tha* is his calf, and the letter *da* is said to be his left foot; the letter *dha* is proclaimed to be all the toes, while the nails are not so described. ||25||
The syllable *pa* is proclaimed as the right side, *pha* as the left; *ba* is said to be the back, and *bha* is remembered as the belly. (26)

The syllable *ma* is the supreme heart, characterized by universal delusion; beginning from there is the wrath of the Lord. The syllable *na* is designated as the nails, while the syllable *ña* is also the nails. The syllable *ḍa* is the hips, and by the syllable *ṇa* are the nails. The two groups of consonants (*ta* and *tha*) are the buttocks; the syllable *ya* is indeed the skin, and *ra* is proclaimed to be the blood. (27)
The letter *la* is proclaimed to be the flesh of the God of gods; *va* is celebrated as the sinew; *śa* is the collection of bones; and *ṣa* is celebrated as the marrow. ||28||
That seed-element (śukradhātu) of the Lord, who is the source of the origin of the world, is the letter *ha*; the letter *kṣa*, however, is said to be wrath (*krodha*). ||29||
Thus, O Goddess, these *mātṛkās* reside briefly within the entire body of Bhairava, performing both creation and dissolution. (30)
In the Siddhayogeśvarītantra, O fair-faced goddess, the ritual of sakalīkaraṇa, which bestows all accomplishments, has been taught for the sake of pleasing you. (31)
Now I shall describe the means of accomplishment for the Śaktis, which has Bhairava as its locus: having resorted to a cremation ground at night, with a single-pointed mind and concentrated. ||32||
Having drawn an eight-spoked wheel complete with a hub and rim, one should fashion the entire wheel as consisting of the color of royalty (red), and the hub as yellow. ||33||
The rim, however, should be made black and marked everywhere with the [triple] qualities; having thus completed the wheel, his form indeed becomes terrifying. ||34||
There, the Great Being Nīla was adorned with all ornaments, yet clad in the directions as his only garment; he possessed a single-pointed mind and was entirely devoid of companions. ||35||
Then, one should worship her as she resides there in her own form, seated upon the pericarp of the lotus in the space of the heart. 36.
Then, O Goddess, having mentally performed [the rites] according to rule and in due order, he subsequently poured red and white [substances] into the consecrated water.
Having consecrated it there with the supreme weapon-mantra, one should worship the excellent deity in the form of Bhairava, illuminated by the khaṭvāṅga, within the navel.
In the form that will be described, he has a great preta as his seat; his body consists of the Mothers and their attendants; he is unborn, the self-existent source of the universe.
Then, with the royal [seeds] and the fire-seeds situated in the spokes, [the deities were established] in their own forms, as well as by the respective seats of the Goddess.
O Great Goddess, they are established as objects of worship in the spokes according to the rule: Brāhmī resides in the *ka*-group, and Vaiṣṇavī in the *ca*-group. 41.

Māheśvarī resides in the *ṭa*-group; she who belongs to Yama should be worshipped with *ta* and so forth. Kaumārī, adorned with a serpent-bracelet, one should worship her with water for the feet (*pādya*). ||42||
In the *yavarga*, Vāsavī is located; there, by means of the syllables beginning with *śa*, she is Karṇamoṭī. This supreme power, Aghoreśī, should be employed in anger. ||43||
One should worship that Goddess, the supreme leader of the universe, who is associated with the god Bhairava of immeasurable luster, who acts for the welfare of the world. 44.
Having prepared various kinds of food offerings and having worshipped with diligence that [goddess] who bestows all fruits in her own form, ||45||
Having thus worshipped with effort according to the rules using fragrant flowers and divine, sweet-smelling incenses, he should remain stationed in the southern direction.
Whether standing or sitting, firm and established in the heroic posture (vīrāsana), perfectly motionless, one should recite the Goddess with a single-pointed mind, absorbed in her. ||47||
Then, through supreme devotion, one certainly beholds her in her own true form; thereafter, one should cause the respectful offering (argha) to be presented. 48.
O Goddess, having filled his joined palms with flowers produced from his left side while reciting the supreme mantra, he then bestows it upon him.
O beloved, having clearly performed this rite, there is no doubt that they will grant whatever desires are wished for in the mind or their own wealth. 50.
O Great Goddess, when endowed with these limbs, she bestows [boons] in this way; of this there is no doubt. Thus the goddess Parāparā becomes the giver of boons during the three nights. 51.

The first [part] of the Navarātra is indeed [performed] with a Sadrātra; the latter [part], which bestows all goals, one should perform according to the ritual rules and mantras of the Goddess. ||52||

The Goddess said: "O Lord, I have heard all this from you in brief regarding the supreme pervasiveness; now explain, according to the proper method, the auspicious rule concerning the higher and the lower."
Bhairava said: Now hear the procedure for the practice of the Supreme-Non-Supreme (Parāparā), by which, when performed, practitioners achieve success in all rites. ||2||
Having drawn an eight-spoked wheel according to the previously mentioned procedure, the wise one should worship Bhairava as before, surrounded by the Mothers. ||3||

The knower of mantras should recite and meditate upon the goddess seated on his lap; he should recite one hundred thousand times according to the rule, and thereafter he should perform the fire-oblation (homa). ||4||
The Mahāphalguṣahoma consists of three thousand oblations multiplied by three; one should perform it in a terrifying cremation ground, entirely devoid of companions. ||5||

At the conclusion of the fire sacrifice, the wise practitioner, reciting the supreme mantra, beholds the Goddess, both transcendent and immanent, stationed within the fire; having taken the blood into a skull-cup, he gazes upon her.

Then, for the sake of accomplishing one's desired aim, the *argha* offering should be given; once the *argha* has been offered, one should pray to the beloved Goddess who is esteemed by the Mistress of Yoga. (7)
She grants him Pātāla or other supernatural attainments; having bestowed all these, or her own power, she vanishes from sight.
Or else, O fair-faced one, it is [the power] of Bhairava himself, the immutable, which is illuminated by that very [power] at the beginning through the indirect path alone. (19)

Having performed the sacrifice, one should then worship the limbs situated in the cardinal and intermediate directions; thereafter, in the spokes, one should worship the group of eight beginning with Aghorī.
One should arrange the mantras for those [deities] according to the divided goddess Parāparā; one should first worship the Mistress of the Gods, Aghorā, who bestows auspiciousness.
In the southeast is Parāghorā; in the southwest is Ghorarūpā, facing south; in the northwest is Ghorī; and again in the western spoke is Vāruṇī. ||12||
One should place the goddess Bhīmā there, and again the terrifying Bhīṣaṇī in the northwest; Vamanī in the north, and Pibanī in the domain of Īśa (the northeast).

Having thus worshipped according to the ritual procedure and having consecrated his own body with the sakalīkaraṇa rite, he should then project the Goddess Parāparā, who resides within his heart, [into the deity]. ||14||

Afterwards, one should perform the placement of the eight [mantras] beginning with Aghora along the path starting from the head; by this mere act of placement, one directly attains the state of Bhairava. ||15||

Having performed the ritual placement (vinyāsa) of the limbs and worshipped the Goddess who is both supreme and non-supreme, the practitioner of mantra, standing in a cremation ground and naked as the directions, should recite the mantra twenty thousand times.

One should perform the worship day by day according to the previously described rite, until the conclusion of the recitation; thereafter, one should have the fire-oblation performed as before. Thus one beholds the Goddess and shall become a possessor of the aforementioned accomplishments. ||17||
Alternatively, in a solitary place or in a delightful house, the practitioner, having performed breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), should practice the mantra for thirty-six [units]. ||18||
One should purify the hands with this very [mantra], and thereafter, one must certainly perform the rite for the Navātman in the form of Bhairava according to the prescribed rule. ||19||
Then, by means of his own mantra, he should install the Goddess Parāparā in her own form, seated upon the pericarp-throne.
Endowed with the five limbs, he should then assign the eight [deities] beginning with Aghorī to their respective places, and thereafter worship the Goddess.
Having meditated upon the wheel according to the rule, one should fix the trident there; likewise, a lotus upon the trident—one should worship her situated therein. ||22||

The practitioner should place the Great Goddess together with her limbs and worship those limbs; furthermore, the mantra-reciter should worship the eight [deities] beginning with Aghorī on the petals of the lotus, and again on the spokes according to the rule.
With fragrant incense and flowers, and with delightful lamps, one should offer various kinds of food offerings and commence the fire ritual.
Alternatively, by means of a goat smeared three times, or likewise with earth, there should be a homa of mahāphalgu; this is remembered as correctly bestowing success. ||25||
O beloved Mistress of the God of Gods, for practitioners of mantra, success in all rites is achieved by means of sesame seeds, or rice, or even fish and meat. (26)

At the conclusion of the fire sacrifice (homa), one should perform the recitation (japa) one hundred and eight times more. [The mantra is: "O Supreme One! You who abide in the heart, you who worship the image, you who are in the wheel, in the mouth, ending in the house of accomplishment, in the hand; ninefold, yours, the selves, in this, the supreme, seated in the seat; endowed with the five limbs, the five-limbed one, together with the equal, the unequal, today, he should join, he should separate; the wheel, in the wheel, the rule, the ruled, easily, surely; above, upon, the station, the station, limb, limb, joined, unjoined, each in its own place, the established ones; by the practitioner, by the three mantras; first, respected, again and again; in the many spokes, the method, the method; with lamps, shining, with dramas, I delight; with the triple-smeared, the abandoned, with the goat, the goat; O Goddess of Gods! a hundred, equal, with eight, with eight, the further, the interval; there, at the junction of day and night, he performs it—he shall bring the lord of the earth under his control. ||27||

Whether one should apply [the mantra], perform oblations, or recite it with a concentrated mind, one quickly becomes successful; there is no need for hesitation in this matter. One should also perform the withdrawal of one's own mantra into one's own heart. (29)

The twilight [is] the earth; the back [is] the back; of the spotted one, for six months, the exit, O Sovereign; the Sovereign, the purpose, the purpose, the purpose—along with, along with, she is worshipped; she worships in worship; let him mutter, let him mutter, being composed; being composed, the purpose, the consideration of what is to be done and what is not to be done, from consideration. Now, furthermore, as to how one should accomplish the Goddess, the Mistress of all the Lords of Yoga: that is as follows—the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), which is the cause for the sake of all accomplishments. 1.
Thus it is said in brief; listen with one-pointed mind to that. First, one should purify the body by means of three breath-controls (prāṇāyāma). ||2||
One should likewise apply the other [breath-control], and after that, withdrawal; then, having burnt away the body, one should fashion the body of knowledge (vidyādeha). ||3||
One should first fashion a body resembling the form of Bhairava with the ninefold self (navātman), and subsequently perform the assignment of the limbs and so forth in due order.
Thus, that Bhairava himself, manifest within his heart, should place the supreme [deity] and perform the ritual assignment of the limbs (*aṅganyāsa*) in his own very form. ||5||
Having thus become the self of all, one should perform sacrifice, which grants the accomplishment of all aims; then, upon the wheel provided with spokes, nave, and rim.
In that [place], which was the color of vermilion, resembling the hibiscus flower, like the blossom of the pomegranate tree, and similar to the indragopaka insect; ||7||

One should worship Bhairava, who resides in the center of the navel, and another [deity] situated in his lap, according to the prescribed method; then one should again install that [deity] as distinct.
To the east, south, southwest, and between the northwest and northeast—these are designated as the spokes; one should worship the goddesses residing therein. 9.
One should worship the goddess mentioned previously with the first [syllable] in the east; one should proceed toward the south-west with the great goddess situated in the second.

When three hundred thousand recitations have been performed with the previously mentioned substances for the Guru, then one should first purify the Supreme (Parā) Kuṇḍa, which belongs to Īśvarīśvarī, Īśvarī, and Īśvarī; having purified it, one should join [the mantras], and with the Aparā [Kuṇḍa] one should fight [the obstacles] by means of the Navātman, not by the [ordinary] self. Bhairava [is established] in Bhairava; Parā is in the Nyāsa of Parā, and the Nyāsa is essentially the Ātman. Then, from that, in the region resembling the navel, [one sees] those resembling a pomegranate (*dāḍima*), appearing like a pomegranate, in the region resembling that, in the lap (*utsaṅga*). Having reached the lap of Parā, who is distinct, she is in the southwest (*nairṛtya*) and in the north (*saumya*). The spokes and directions are seen; the Goddess is in her place, as declared. Bhadrā, Gopati, Ḍāgī, Guhā, Gopanakhā, Balā, Biḍālī, Kālarātrī, Bhaṭṭā, and likewise Nāgeśvarī. || 13 ||

Harī, Bhānumatī, Śrībalā, Kapilaprabhā, the renowned Muktāvalī, and likewise the other, Bhānumātā. ||19||

For thus, subjugation and attraction, as well as restraint and favor, and affection for all people—these and other such accomplishments are considered inferior. (11)
Thus, having been questioned by you, I have explained everything without exception; now, O Goddess, hear their most secret characteristic. ||12||
Viśvā, Viśveśvarī, Hāraudrī, Vīranāyikā, Ambā, Gurvī—by these names she is thus celebrated. (13)

The supreme source of all sciences (*vidyā*), according to the *Siddhayogeśvarīmata*, is the Goddess who abides in the Supreme; O God, she is established by you through absorption (*laya*). O Goddess, those who have fallen into calamity are rescued by you, the Goddess, again and again. What is accomplishment (*siddhi*)? What is curiosity? What is the earth-born? What is the means (*sadhana*)? What is the support (*sādhāra*)? Of what kind are they? Of what kind are they for them? By whom [is it attained], O Maheśvara? By whom [is it attained], O Maheśvarī? By the practitioner (*sādhaka*) and the practitioneress (*sādhakī*). By which [means]? By the masters of yoga (*yogeśvarī*) and the yoginīs. O wielder of the Pināka bow, [I ask] in due order, from the womb (*yoni*) in due order, from the womb in due order, regarding the fruit (*phala*) without contradiction. From the absence of contradiction, [there arise] the powers such as atomization (*animā*) and so forth, up to liberation (*mokṣa*). These are remembered as the highest. In the netherworld (*pātāla*), the perfected ones (*siddha*) are established. O Goddess, [they attain] the state of being subject to the Goddess. The first ones are the lowest. Having been asked about the universe (*viśva*), the universe was explained. Hara, Rudrī, Mahogrā, Ambā, Gurvī—thus is the womb (*yoni*) declared, the power of Rudra (*rudraśakti*). She is Mātṛkā, the possessor of all eyes. (14)
From this supreme tantra have emerged these [teachings] from the mouth of the Yoginī: that which is called Vīra, the Essence of the Siddhas, and beyond that, the Five Nectars. ||15||
The Viśvādya, the network of Yoginīs, that which is called Kāla, the Khecara, as well as the Sādhana, the Savara, the Tilaka, and the supreme Hṛdaya. ||16||
The Vidyāpīṭha, the Śiraccheda, the Mahāsammohana, as well as the Nayottara, the Mahāraudra, and the Rudrayāmala. ||17||
The Brahmayāmala and another, likewise the Viṣṇuyāmala, the Skandayāmala, and also the Umāyāmala. ||18||
O Caṇḍākṣī, these and other tantras, divided into sixty-four, have emerged here according to the *Siddhayogeśvarīmata*. (19)

This secret of the *khecarīs* has not been told by me to anyone; it was requested by you, O Mistress of Gods, and thus it has been told by me, O fair-eyed one. These twelve locations of the *sūtras* have been described in the *Amṛta*. (20)
Hereafter, I shall proclaim the characteristics that fulfill all desires, by which a brother or a sister can be recognized without any doubt. ||21||
Her face should be seen to be perfectly round on all sides; her mouth should have a beard, her eyebrows should be long, and her eyes should be very beautiful. (22)
She who loves white garments, who is gentle, unshakeable, truthful in speech, and always fond of the sound of Vedic recitation, is proclaimed as Brāhmaṇī. ||23||
The lotus mudrā should be presented, or alternatively the upward-pointing mudrā; furthermore, the deer skin and the water-pot are prescribed as the counter-mudrās. ||24||
O fair-faced one, on the tenth lunar day among those festivals, a lotus is drawn in the home of women born of Brahmin families who are masters of yoga.
She will undoubtedly attain success even among the formidable Brahmā and Īśāna; by following this rite for just one month, she will then become a follower of one's desires.
She has long lips and large eyes, with reddish-brown pupils; she is wealthy, fortunate, blessed, fair-complexioned, and possesses the fragrance of the campaka flower. ||27||
Long, long and formidable, and fond of variegated garments—these three lines situated on the forehead rest upon the upward parting of the hair. ||28||
Established in the practice of celibacy, she both laughs and rejoices; she always delights in stories of those who have died on the field of battle. (29)
Upon seeing such a woman, one should display the trident mudrā, contract the left foot, and likewise display the bow. ||30||
Indeed, they give the reversal with the left hand and the counter-seal; this occurs on the fourth, the fifth, the ninth, and likewise the eleventh. (31)
The fourteenth day, the new moon, and the full moon in both fortnights—these indeed belong to the lineage of Maheśvarī; they are devoted to the meditation on Śarva.
They grant boons to the foremost of practitioners and bestow the fruits of all desires; indeed, they act for the sake of accomplishing every wish. ||33||
When two pits are seen situated on her cheeks, and she is reddish-fair with tawny eyes like those of a lion, [she is a woman of ill omen]. //34//
His hair is curly and even, he wears a cloth turban on his head, and a single line is visible upon his forehead. (35)
She should be known as having a long neck, long limbs, and red hair; she always delights in red, yellow, or blue garments. (36)

She laughs and sports, yet she becomes angry for no apparent reason. She has dimples on both cheeks, a face like that of Brahmā and Īśa, and protruding lips. Her garments and her face are turned upward, and she stands with her feet raised high. A woman who displays such a *darśa-mudrā* is a servant of Maheśvara. These women grant boons; they have dimples visible on both cheeks, their hair is fair, curly, and even, and such a woman is fickle-minded and takes delight in quarrels. (37)
Having seen such a young woman, one should display the *śakti-mudrā*, and the *ghaṇṭā-mudrā* should also be offered as the second with great care. ||38||
Indeed, by turning it to the left, she gives the counter-seal; she is the sixth joint, and women born of her are those of the Kaumāra family. ||39||
She who has arisen from the lineage of Kārttikeya bestows success despite the six defects; when she is pleased, she grants the tradition that fulfills all desires. ||40||
She has pendulous breasts, beautiful shanks, a fine forehead, and speaks eloquently; she may be black, dark as a blue lotus, or dark like a mung bean. ||41||
She who is flat-nosed, short, and has thick calves, should always wear yellow garments hanging down over her shoulders and neck. ||42||
Having seen such a young woman, one should show her the conch; or else, one should again show her the second [mudrā], the wheel-mudrā. ||43||
And by turning with the left hand, she gives the counter-seal; that is the twelfth festival (parvanī) among them, and their wheel is drawn in the house. //44//
This is the characteristic of the Vaiṣṇava yoginīs, as well as all the objects of desire and happiness for the diligent practitioner. 45.
However, according to the *Siddhayogeśvarīmata*, those [mantras] of the Yoginīs and Vaiṣṇavīs should always be known by practitioners who desire to attain the power of moving through the sky. ||46||
Her entire body was covered in hair, her eyes were blackish-brown, her form was terrifying and deformed, she was fierce, and her teeth were large. 47.
Long-lipped, dark-complexioned, with eyes like a crow's and a broken nose, she was skilled in dance and music; she was cloud-colored and possessed great luster. ||48||

Upon seeing such a woman, one should display the fang-mudrā (*damṣṭrā-mudrā*). She is particularly fickle-minded and takes delight in quarrels. Upon seeing such a woman, one should cause the spear-mudrā (*śakti-mudrā*) to be given; the bell-mudrā (*ghaṇṭā-mudrā*) should also be presented with effort as the second. The counter-mudrā (*pratimudrā*) is prescribed with the left hand. She is short, has thick calves, is fond of pleasant garments, always wears her cloth draped over her shoulder, and upon seeing such a woman, one should cause the discus-mudrā (*cakra-mudrā*) to be given. The conch-mudrā (*śaṅkha-mudrā*) should be presented with effort as the second; the counter-mudrā is prescribed with the left hand. On the fourteenth lunar day (*parvan*), a vajra is drawn in her house. She is hairy in all her limbs, has dark-brown eyes, is terrifying, deformed, fierce, thick-lipped, thick-jawed, pendulous-lipped, black-complexioned, hollow-eyed, and flat-nosed. She is skilled in dance and music, cloud-colored, and captivating. She is restless in rhythm and in quarrels. Such is the woman; her mudrā is the mudrā for that lunar day. Her kinsmen, O Kārttikeya, are all eloquent. She is dark-complexioned and flat-nosed, with a thick shoulder. Upon seeing such a woman, the conch-mudrā is the second; the turning-mudrā (*vartana-mudrā*) is drawn in the house as a sign by those desiring victory. One should show her the fang, the bone, the broken nose, or the lack of luster; then, without hesitation, one should show her the fang or even the staff (*daṇḍa*).
Bestowing boons upon the practitioner, she leads him to union with Śiva; at the end of the aeon, she is the destructive thunderbolt.
Their reversal is undoubtedly by means of the left-hand mudrās; they should always be recognized as those who sport in the world of Bhūrloka. 51.
Or one may display the staff (daṇḍa) without hesitation; when joined with the mudrā of destruction at the end of the aeon, those who have mastered it sport in the world of mortals.

by means of this, the activities of Bhairava are fulfilled through the digits of the entire stream, numbering ten million and four hundred thousand.

O Goddess of gods, my laughter issued forth for that reason;

O illustrious Goddess of gods, this understanding of the mantra has been accomplished; indeed, O divine one, this is proclaimed as laughter among the gods and sages.
Furthermore, O Goddess Maheśvarī, the kings of colors do not know how he moves everywhere— the colorless one who possesses the form of all colors.
The enjoyer is proclaimed in all the tantras as the substratum of the elements, the senses, and the qualities, by way of the relationship between the container and the contained.
In brief, I have revealed this entire reality;
it is proclaimed as a complete work of one thousand three hundred verses, the *Siddhayogeśvarītantra*, a secret and most excellent of the excellent.

The laughter of the sixteen [streams] is Śaṅkara; Bhairava’s own single task is performed by the digits (*kalābhiḥ*) of the flow; he played with the end-maker (*antaka*); by that very laughter, O Goddess, this unlettered reality (*avarṇa-tattva*) among the *saddha*s is fulfilled (*pūrṇa*). Bhairava said: Now, O Goddess, this secret mantra, which destroys all sins, [is attained] through the study of the *praṇava* and also through the realization of the meaning of what has been heard.
O illustrious one, by means of retaining [this], or writing it down, or even by remembering it,
one is released from terrible sins such as the killing of a Brahmin and the like.
Even those who strike their fathers and mothers and are established outside the bounds of Dharma become heroes in this [system]; how much more so, then, men who are practitioners?
The Siddhayogeśvarī Tantra bestows grace upon all; therefore, O Goddess, this Tantra is worshipped by the power of Rudra.
O illustrious lady, this *Siddhayogeśvarītantra*, the seat of knowledge (*vidyāpīṭha*),
has been declared to you as the very essence, honored by heroes.
There is no knowledge equal to this, nor is there any fruit equal to this:
the *Svacchandabhairava* Tantra, obtained by Bhairavī from Bhairava.
From him Garuḍaprapta received it; from him Śukra obtained it; from him Kaca acquired it through the medicinal powder.
Therefore, that which was attained by Rāma has been made manifest in the world; whoever hears it, reads it, or cultivates meditative absorption upon it [attains the same].
He becomes a lord of yoga, augmented by the splendor of Rudra; he is the support of the elements, the senses, and the qualities—the omniscient one who partakes in the fruits [of action].
Therefore, the Tantra must not be given to one who follows an unjust path; for this is the command of the great-souled Lord Bhairava.
Having renounced wealth and even life itself, and not disclosing his secret, the Guru should bestow [the initiation] upon that disciple who possesses devotion equal to that for the power of Rudra.
Having emerged from Ayodhyā, it passed from mouth to mouth through the lineage of gurus; previously kept secret by the God, it was made even more secret by the Goddess.

It is self-willed, protected by the Ṛṣis, and always guarded by Rāma; it has reached a state more secret than the secrets of the Yoginīs and the Gurus. If it were merely secret, there would be accomplishment, but because it is made even more secret than that [it is supreme].

The remover [of obstacles], the practitioner, the unborn, the one revealed as Garuḍa, the Lord, the one celebrated by the gods, the one who has transcended the elements, senses, and qualities; the knower of the stream [of consciousness] from the mouth of the Guru, the one who holds his own will, the leader of the Gaṇas, the fortunate one, the one whose power has gone to the Blessed One, the face of Ayodhyā, the deity, the swift attainment of success—[this is for those] desiring the fruits declared in the Kalpa. [This occurs] here, by means of the Power, according to the Rule, for some, in the Śaiva [tradition], in rites for specific desires, here, [the attainment of] mantras, the secret mandala, and the one who knows the Sūtra.

those who are non-terrible (aghorāḥ), who bestow grace, dispel the darkness within the body, and grant auspiciousness through their benevolence— they are celebrated as the Aghoras.
